lineLayout: 3-liner, A / A' / B / C risers, upper D cascading into C

published._comment: Manufacturer specification. Measurements, not tuning. The main-line counts fix the cascade topology in SuspensionGraph.cpp; total line length is a check on the derived rest lengths, not an input.

assumed._comment: Not published. Each carries the reason it exists and what would replace it. Rest lengths are not listed here: they are measured from the Level 1 geometry at the design pose, so the wing hangs where its own shape puts it.

designIncidenceRad.why: Root chord incidence in the harness frame at the unloaded design pose, 5 deg nose-up. Sets where the rest lengths are cut, so it fixes hands-up trim incidence. Replace with the manufacturer's rigging angle, or by fitting Level 4 trim speed.

cascadeSplitFraction.why: How far up the riser-to-canopy run each cascade junction sits. Governs how much of the load path is main line versus upper gallery, and therefore total stretch. Digitising the line plan replaces it.

brakeCascadeSplitFraction.why: Same, for the brake fan, which cascades lower so the fan can spread along the trailing edge.

mainLineDiameterM.why: Sheathed main line. Sets axial stiffness and drag area.

upperLineDiameterM.why: Unsheathed upper gallery, the usual construction on a wing of this class.

brakeLineDiameterM.why: Brake lines run heavier than uppers because they are handled.

lineModulusPa.why: Effective axial modulus of sheathed Dyneema-class line. UHMWPE fibre is near 100 GPa; a sheathed, spliced, bedded-in line behaves considerably softer. Order-of-magnitude from the cordage literature; a pull test on a real line replaces it.

lineDensityKgM3.why: UHMWPE bulk density. Only sets line weight, which is what makes the cascade junctions droop.

carabinerSeparationM.why: Carabiner spacing across the harness. Level 3 replaces it with harness geometry.

hipTravelM.why: How far a seated pilot moves their CG sideways at full weight shift. Level 3 replaced the earlier travel and tilt stand-ins with this: the mass moves, the harness rolls under it, and the carabiners take unequal shares. Measure it on a simulator rig to replace it.

chestStrapM.why: Chest strap between riser attachment points. Narrower lets the harness roll further for the same hip movement, so it sets weight-shift authority through geometry rather than through a gain.

brakeSlackM.why: Slack sewn into the brake line at hands-up. Without it the brake line would load at trim, which is the failure the exit gate checks for.

brakeTravelM.why: Brake handle travel at full input, applied as a rest-length change rather than a moment (guiding rule 4).

derived._comment: Computed by BuildSuspensionGraph from the geometry and the design pose, recorded so a change shows up in review. See SuspensionTests for the checks.

safety: Simulator content. Line lengths and stiffness are unvalidated research estimates and must not be used for rigging, repair or airworthiness.
